newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo's Kabila replaces opposition minister.
newsitem.headline: Congo's Kabila replaces opposition minister.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila has made his first cabinet change since seizing power in the former Zaire, replacing one of two ministers from the the civilian opposition, state television said.
The television reported on Saturday night that Kabila had sacked Civil Service Minister Justine Kasa-Vubu, a vocal supporter of radical opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi.

She has been replaced by a close associate of Tshisekedi, Paul Kapita. No reason was given for the removal of Kasa-Vubu, a daughter of the Central African country's first president, the late Joseph Kasa-Vubu.
Kabila has faced strong opposition from Tshisekedi's camp since excluding the populist politician from his government after overthrowing former dictator Mobutu Sese Seko in May.
Tshisekedi's Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS), disassociated itself from the initial appointment of Kasa-Vubu and another member, Paul Bandoma, Kabila's Agriculture Minister.
UDPS again denounced Saturday's nomination.

"The appointment of Kapita is an isolated act. It's his own business. The UDPS has no representative in Kabila's government," Tshidekedi's senior aide Mukende wa Mulumba told Reuters. "Those who join Kabila's team do it for themselves."
Mukendi added that both Kasa-Vubu and Bandoma were no longer members of Tshisekedi's party.

"The so-called UDPS ministers have never received the green light of the party. But we're not surprised, it was predictable. We knew that they were people among us who were planning to join Kabila," he said.

Earlier on Saturday an opposition leader called for a round-table meeting with Kabila to discuss power-sharing and hinted the opposition might resort to violence if the talks did not get off the ground.

Roger Lumbala, leader of the Rally for the Congolese People (RPC), told Reuters in an interview that the meeting should gather together the "main political forces" in the renamed Democratic Republic of the Congo.

"There are two ways of conducting a struggle. The thing is to choose between the political and the armed struggle. If they oppose the round-table meeting, we will feel free to resort to violence to put our ideas forward," Lumbala said.
"We've set no deadline yet for the talks. We want to negotiate. But if President Kabila's door is still closed, he will bear the consequences," he said.
Lumbala's RPC is mainly led by former exiles who returned home after Mobutu's fall. The ousted dictator, who ruled for 32 years, is ailing with cancer in Morocco.
Although Kabila has promised elections in two years, he has banned political activity and his forces have stamped down firmly on any opposition attempts to hold protest marches.

The 24-member cabinet is dominated by members of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, whose guerrillas launched Kabila to power with a seven-month armed offensive from the vast country's eastern border.

The television said Kabila had appointed Kanu Mutumba Iserere to the new post of deputy minister for public enterprises. Kabila assumed direct responsibility for the ministry, which will oversee state interests in mining.
Kanu's political background is not known.
The new central bank governor is Jean-Claude Masangu Mulongo, the former head of the Kinshasa branch of Citibank.
The television said Kabila had named a Paul Kapanga as ambassador to the United Nations, but there were no other details about the nominee.
